LESSON: PROHIBITIONS IN ISLAM • DRUG ABUSE

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Akhlaq (Moral Teachings)
Topic 5.3: Prohibitions in Islam • Drug abuse
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Prohibitions in Islam • Drug abuse, part of Akhlaq (Moral Teachings) in Grade 7 ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION.

Key inquiry question: What causes drug abuse? 2. What are the effects of drug abuse in the society? 3. What are the possible remedies for drug abuse?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. describe the effects of drug abuse for healthy living,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Prohibitions in Islam • Drug abuse in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. examine the rationale behind the prohibition of drugs as a way of fostering positive character formation,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Prohibitions in Islam • Drug abuse in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. explain remedies for drug abuse for a healthy and morally upright society,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Prohibitions in Islam • Drug abuse in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. abstain from abusing drugs to earn Allah’s pleasure,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Prohibitions in Islam • Drug abuse in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. acknowledge the rationale for the prohibition of drugs for the growth and development of the nation.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Prohibitions in Islam • Drug abuse in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. describe the effects of drug abuse for healthy living,

   Prohibitions in Islam • Drug abuse helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. examine the rationale behind the prohibition of drugs as a way of fostering positive character formation,

   Prohibitions in Islam • Drug abuse helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. explain remedies for drug abuse for a healthy and morally upright society,

   Prohibitions in Islam • Drug abuse helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. abstain from abusing drugs to earn Allah’s pleasure,

   Prohibitions in Islam • Drug abuse helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. acknowledge the rationale for the prohibition of drugs for the growth and development of the nation.

   Prohibitions in Islam • Drug abuse helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

F. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. list down some types of drugs bhang, heroin, cocaine, khat etc),

2. discuss the effects of drug abuse in the society and present on charts/PowerPoint,

3. search and watch video clips/search on available newspapers, books, magazines, and journals on the effects of drug abuse and deduce lessons,

4. use digital devices/ available Islamic books to research the rationale behind the prohibition, of drugs in Islam and make notes

5. research on the possible remedies for drug abuse and make posters,

6. depict through skits the effects of drug abuse in the society,

7. research on the effects and remedies of drug abuse and develop portfolios, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. list down some types of drugs bhang, heroin, cocaine, khat etc),
2. discuss the effects of drug abuse in the society and present on charts/PowerPoint,
3. search and watch video clips/search on available newspapers, books, magazines, and journals on the effects of drug abuse and deduce lessons,
4. use digital devices/ available Islamic books to research the rationale behind the prohibition, of drugs in Islam and make notes
5. research on the possible remedies for drug abuse and make posters,
6. depict through skits the effects of drug abuse in the society,
7. research on the effects and remedies of drug abuse and develop portfolios, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Prohibitions in Islam • Drug abuse together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and Problem-solving research skills are developed when learners research on the possible remedies for drug

abuse.

• Learning to Learn: the skill of seeking advice, information, and support is developed as learners visit a rehabilitation centre

to learn more about the effects and remedies for drug abuse.

• Digital Literacy Skills: the learners interact with digital technology as they use digital devices to research the rationale

behind the prohibition of drugs in Islam.

• Communication and Collaboration: the learners listen and appreciate a talk on drug abuse from a medical expert/NACADA

official.

Values:
Responsibility: enhanced as learners discuss ways of avoiding drug abuse.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Alcohol and substance abuse: the learners watch video clips on the effects of drug abuse.

Link to other Subjects:

Integrated Science: the learners discuss the effects of drug abuse in society.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. describe the effects of drug abuse for healthy living,
2. examine the rationale behind the prohibition of drugs as a way of fostering positive character formation,
3. explain remedies for drug abuse for a healthy and morally upright society,
4. abstain from abusing drugs to earn Allah’s pleasure,
5. acknowledge the rationale for the prohibition of drugs for the growth and development of the nation.

Remember the key question: What causes drug abuse? 2. What are the effects of drug abuse in the society? 3. What are the possible remedies for drug abuse?
